ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances establish the deviation: 9.5 km actually driven against a recommended 8.1 km, a deviation of 1.40 km under POL-RD-22's formula (actual_distance_km minus optimal_distance_km, using the platform's recorded distances). That is 0.40 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance, so this case cannot sit in any within-tolerance no-refund row of POL-RD-24.

The route actually taken is the deviation the rider describes: the trace leaves the recommended PIE line at the Clementi Avenue 6 exit at 08:42:55, runs down Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West, and rejoins at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West at 08:53:16 — the route was changed and the rider's account of it is correct. Catchment not in dispute. (POL-RD-22 uses the trace to show which route was taken and when, not to re-measure distance.)

The driver never informed the rider of the deviation, before it or at the point of it, as POL-RD-21 requires. The trip record's own derived block for POL-RD-21 shows messages_during_trip as an empty list, and in_app_calls is empty too, so there is neither an in-app chat notice nor a recorded verbal one. The deviation occurred at 08:42:55; the chat log contains nothing after 08:36:12.

The rider's single message ("Ok", 08:36:12) cannot be an acknowledgment of the deviation. It replies to the driver's 08:35:52 message about where the car was parked at Westgate, and it was sent six minutes before the deviation at 08:42:55 and before the trip even started at 08:37:22. There is no agreed deviation on this record, so POL-RD-24(a) is not in play.

The driver's own statement in this dispute concedes the notification failure: "Forgot to inform, sorry." Under POL-RD-21 a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established (POL-GEN-26), and in any event the driver does not assert he gave one — he says he forgot. The notification limb fails on the driver's own account as well as on the chat log.

The rider does not need the traffic question resolved in his favour, because it does not change the money. If the LTA advisory is read as justifying the reroute, the driver still failed to inform, which is POL-RD-24(b) — refund of the excess distance fare. If the advisory is not read as intersecting the recommended route, the case is POL-RD-24(d) — refund of the excess distance fare in full. Both rows pay the same figure; the rider's entitlement follows on either reading, and the rider presses the refund row rather than asking the tribunal to resolve the traffic question.

On the traffic limb specifically, POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and the artifact's own derived fields leave intersects_route undetermined (value null, determined_by judge). The rider's submission is that the justification is not established on the artifact as presented, so POL-RD-24(d) is the row the record best fits — but the rider's claim stands on row (b) as well if the judge finds otherwise.

The amount owed is fixed by POL-RD-24's excess-distance formula from the clean ledger: deviation_km 1.40 times per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, with no surge, equals 1.008 SGD, rounded to the cent as 1.01 SGD. The fare breakdown confirms the charge was metered, no surge applied and payment status CHARGED, so the money is still with the driver's side and is recoverable.

The rider asked for 4.00 SGD; the policy's measure is narrower, and the rider presses his claim to 1.01 SGD and no further. The correct outcome is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD under POL-GEN-03 — part of the trip's charge returned — not the whole contested 4.00 SGD, which no row of POL-RD-24 provides. The rider prefers the amount the rules actually give him to an inflated figure that would fail.

No escalation is warranted under POL-GEN-26: every fact the refund rows need is carried by complete evidence. The deviation distance comes from the trip record and the notification failure from the chat log, both assessed COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so nothing is impaired and no fact is missing. The disputed value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final here and the case should be decided, not held.

On this record the deviation is 1.40 km — the trip record's own actual distance of 9.5 km less its recommended 8.1 km, which is the measure POL-RD-22 requires — and 1.40 km is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so some refund is due. But POL-RD-24 fixes what that refund is: the excess distance fare, being the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge. That is 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD, the ledger's own derived figure, against a contested 4.00 SGD. The rider is owed 1.01 SGD and no more; the further 2.99 SGD has no basis either in the fare ledger or in any row of the POL-RD-24 matrix.

The deviation was a response to real congestion, which is what POL-RD-21 permits a driver to reroute for: the LTA advisory in the record reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the Pan-Island Expressway and is valid 08:15:42 to 09:27:22, spanning the whole trip (08:37:22 to 08:55:22) and the 08:42:55 deviation, and HEAVY_TRAFFIC is one of the congestion types POL-RD-23 admits as traffic justification. The advisory's own location wording — 'after Clementi Avenue 6 exit to Clementi Road exit' — names the motorway stretch the recommended route runs to reach its Clementi Road exit, and the platform logged the deviation at 'PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit'; on the record's own road and exit names the advisory sits on the leg the driver left. The record states no carriageway direction for the trip, so nothing in the record sets the advisory off that leg; the record's derived block leaves the single question of intersection to the Judge, and the road, the two exits and the window are all in the record.

The driver does not contest the notice limb of POL-RD-21: the chat log holds two messages, both about the pickup point and both sent before the trip started (08:35:52 and 08:36:12), no message was sent during the trip, and the driver's own statement admits 'Forgot to inform'. The case therefore falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24 — traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — and if the Judge does not find the advisory on the route it falls in row (d); either row returns the same thing, the excess distance fare, so the outcome is the same 1.01 SGD whichever way that question goes. Under POL-GEN-03 that is a PARTIAL_REFUND of part of the charge; it is not the whole 4.00 SGD the rider asks for.

POL-RD-24's measure is distance-only and without surge, so the rider cannot assemble 4.00 SGD out of the other ledger lines: the 18.0 minutes of time fare, the 2.80 SGD base fare, the 0.90 SGD platform fee and the 1.00 SGD ERP charge are all outside the formula (surge is 1.0 and surge_amount 0.0, so the no-surge rule is satisfied on the facts). The ERP in particular was recorded on the Pan-Island Expressway at 08:40:36 via gantry ERP-42, two minutes before the 08:42:55 deviation, and the optimal route carries the same 1.00 SGD toll, so the reroute added nothing there. The single recoverable item on this fare breakdown is the 1.01 SGD excess distance fare.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the record decides this case, and both sides in the end read it the same way. On POL-RD-22 the deviation is the platform's own recorded distances, 9.5 km actually driven minus the recommended 8.1 km = 1.40 km (EV-TRIP-05004), and 1.40 km is over the 1.0 km tolerance. On POL-RD-21 the driver did not inform the rider before or at the point of the deviation: the trip record's messages-during-trip list and in_app_calls are empty, the chat log (EV-CHAT-05004) holds only the two pre-trip pickup messages (08:35:52 and 08:36:12) against a deviation at 08:42:55, and the driver's own statement concedes it ('Forgot to inform, sorry'). The rider's 'Ok' at 08:36:12 cannot be an acknowledgment of a deviation that had not yet happened. So this is not row (a) of POL-RD-24, and the within-tolerance no-refund rows (c) and (e) do not apply either. What is owed is fixed by POL-RD-24's excess-distance formula: deviation distance 1.40 km x the metered rate 0.72 SGD/km (EV-FARE-05004) = 1.008, rounded to the cent as 1.01 SGD, which is the ledger's own derived excess_distance_fare_sgd. I note the one open question in the record: whether the LTA HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory (EV-ADVIS-05004-01) intersects the recommended route, so as to make the reroute traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. It does not change the money, because if it is justified the case is row (b) and if it is not the case is row (d), and both rows refund the same excess distance fare. I therefore do not need to resolve it, and neither side asked me to. The rider asked for 4.00 SGD, but POL-RD-24's measure is distance-only and without surge: the 2.80 SGD base fare, the 3.24 SGD time fare, the 0.90 SGD platform fee and the 1.00 SGD ERP charge all sit outside the formula, and the ERP was incurred on the PIE at 08:40:36, before the 08:42:55 deviation, and is carried on the optimal route too. The rider is owed 1.01 SGD, not 4.00 SGD and not nothing, so under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD. Every artifact relied on is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so my confidence is not capped below 1.0; I set it at 0.90 against the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for a route deviation. The disputed value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so this AI ruling is final; there is no safety flag and no fraud flag, no escalation under POL-GEN-26 arises because every fact the refund row needs is carried by complete evidence, and no clause adds a referral. The 1.01 SGD is returned to the rider; the driver keeps the rest of the metered fare.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
